title: add RAG agent quickstarts, tool-calling samples, and docs site updates
author: Jordan Liu
description: This PR introduces a set of RAG (retrieval-augmented generation) agent quickstarts, tool-calling examples, and corresponding docs site updates to make it easy for engineers to prototype agents that combine retrieval, tool-calling, and structured outputs. Motivation: several customers and internal teams requested canonical quickstarts that demonstrate 1) how to wire up a simple RAG pipeline with our embeddings + store, 2) an agent pattern that calls external tools (search, calendar, and an internal ticketing API) via the open tool-calling interface, and 3) recommended prompt/response serializers for structured outputs. Changes include new example projects (redwood-examples/agents/rag-quickstart and redwood-examples/agents/tool-calling-sample), RAG template files under redwood-examples/templates/rag, a docs site quickstart page and navigation updates, and a small SDK usage snippet for Python and TypeScript. Checklist: - [x] add RAG templates and example agent code - [x] add tool-calling sample that demonstrates search/calendar/ticket workflows - [x] docs quickstart page with copy, code samples, and diagrams - [x] unit tests for example helpers (mock store + mock tool clients) - [x] CI linting and docs build green Notes: - The description and code samples are intentionally minimal and focused on the developer experience; production considerations (auth, retries, rate limiting) are documented in the new 'Productionizing agents' section. - Examples reference Linear ticket ENG-4821 for the agent playbook and PM-119 for product acceptance criteria. - Docs site changes update the left-hand nav under 'Quickstarts > Agents' and add a new 'RAG templates' subsection. See the migration notes in the release_notes field below for how this affects existing quickstarts.
